newsitem.title: UK: BCC SAYS RATE RISE WILL HURT BRITISH EXPORTERS.
newsitem.headline: BCC SAYS RATE RISE WILL HURT BRITISH EXPORTERS.

text.p: The British Chambers of Commerce said the Bank of England's decision to raise rates on Thursday would send Britain's exporters reeling.

"This is the last thing Britain's exporters and their suppliers need at this time. If sterling continues to rise, fuelled by these hikes, the result will be highly damaging to profits, investments and jobs," said Ian Peters, deputy director general of the BCC.
The Bank of England announced a quarter point rise in interest rates to 7.0 percent on Thursday, after a two-day monetary policy committee meeting. This was the fourth such rise in as many months.
The BCC said the rise was not necessary in view of the strength of sterling and the three previous rate rises.

"The bank should assess the combined effects of lower import prices, falling wage inflation, the budget measures, and the previous rises in interest rates before making any further increases," Peters said.
